h2: ECT inspection services in the Boston area: matching the tube technique to the material
html:
ECT inspection services in the Boston area: matching the tube technique to the material

ECT inspection services around Boston are mostly tube work: condensers, chillers, feedwater heaters and process exchangers. The first decision is the tube material, because bobbin eddy current suits copper alloys, stainless and titanium, while carbon-steel tubes need remote field, near-field or ultrasonic IRIS techniques. Atlantis scopes each Massachusetts job around that choice, then mobilises a crew from Houston.

The material-to-technique match Atlantis applies when scoping a bundle:

  • Copper alloy, cupronickel, stainless and titanium tubes: bobbin eddy current to ASME Section V Article 8, with ASTM E690 covering in-situ examination of non-magnetic exchanger tubes.
  • Carbon-steel and other ferromagnetic tubes: remote field testing to ASTM E2096, or near-field testing on finned air-cooler tubes, with IRIS tube inspection to size wall loss the screening finds.
  • Tubesheet faces, rolled joints and U-bends: array or rotating probes where bobbin coverage is weak or crack orientation is a concern.

Fitting tube work into Massachusetts inspection windows. Under 522 CMR 4.05, steam heating boilers built with manholes and handholes get an internal inspection every year and hot-water boilers with them every three years, on top of the annual external. Power boilers under 522 CMR 2.06 are opened annually as well. The owner must cool, drain, clean and open the boiler, and an inspector may refuse a unit that is not ready. Plant engineers in hospitals, campuses and process plants often schedule chiller, condenser and exchanger tube testing into the same shutdown, which means the ECT crew is booked against a date the jurisdiction has effectively already set.

Standards and probes. Each tube size needs its own calibration standard, made from the same material, diameter and wall as the bundle, with machined holes and grooves that set phase and amplitude for the depth calls. Fill factor matters as much: a bobbin probe sized close to the tube bore gives clean signals, while one undersized to pass dents or deposits trades away sensitivity. Tube cleaning before testing is therefore part of the scope rather than an optional extra, and who does it is settled when the job is quoted.

What the owner receives. A tubesheet map, an indication list sorted by depth band and location, and the calibration standard record for each probe and frequency set. Plugging and sleeving decisions stay with the owner's engineer; the report gives them the data in a form they can act on. Raw data is supplied in the instrument's native format so the next campaign can compare like with like, and results can be delivered through Atlantis NDT reporting if the plant has no system of its own.

Surface eddy current on aerospace and defence components is a separate service with its own rules: OEM process specifications, conductivity work and NAS 410 personnel requirements, where Atlantis covers Level 3 duties only through an associate.

The national eddy current testing service lists the probe types available, and shutdown inspection describes how crews are staged into an outage. Technicians looking to learn the method can use eddy current testing training and the eddy current simulator. For a Boston-area tube campaign, send the tube schedule and material.
